candidate.title: BSPP
candidate.scope: The BSPP (bisulfite sequencing with padlock probes) row of the assigned Illumina poster schematic, clarified by the cited Deng et al. targeted bisulfite implementation. One target workflow is depicted, with a separate padlock-probe input and no alternative route. HELP-Seq, PBAT and RRBS/scRRBS occupy neighboring rows and are outside this record. This captures the displayed architecture, including its compressed final library-conversion block, rather than all probe-production, normalization or execution details in the paper.

features: Input DNA carries the biological cytosine-methylation pattern; the CpG island is a target example, not a separately isolated molecule.
The leftmost yellow-highlighted CpG-island motif is descriptive; the DNA immediately before Bisulfite conversion is the workflow input.

states.label: DNA with adaptors
features: Final linear, adapter-bearing DNA library derived from the amplified capture products; the endpoint is a straight blue line labeled DNA with adaptors.
The readout carrier is DNA copied from the bisulfite-converted genomic target, rather than native methylated genomic DNA or probe-arm sequence alone.

At a covered genomic cytosine, strand-normalized C versus conversion-derived T (or the complementary A/G distinction) carries the bisulfite methylation readout. Sequencing can associate that base identity with a targeted genomic position to estimate methylation at captured CpGs. The diagram ends at library DNA and does not depict sequencing or a computational-analysis branch.
This is targeted coverage determined by probe placement and capture performance; neither whole-genome coverage nor perfect capture specificity is implied.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Converts the input genomic DNA to the bisulfite-treated template used by the probes. Unmethylated cytosines become uracils; subsequent copying converts this chemical distinction into sequence information.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite-dependent conversion of unmethylated cytosine to uracil, as reported by the primary source.
operations.information_effect: Encodes the original methylation state in conversion-dependent base identity on the genomic template; the original covalent methyl group need not be carried into the eventual PCR library.

operations.label: Hybridize
operations.description: Brings the two arms of a padlock probe into sequence-specific contact with flanking sites on a bisulfite-converted DNA target, leaving an intervening gap.
operations.mechanism: Cooperative binding of the two target-specific capture arms to the template positions that flank the sequence to be copied.
operations.information_effect: Associates the probe backbone and universal-primer sites with a selected genomic locus; it does not yet copy the intervening target sequence.

operations.label: Extension and ligation
operations.description: Extends the probe 3′ end across the target gap on the converted genomic template and ligates the extended end to the probe 5′ end, producing a closed circle containing a target-derived copy.
operations.mechanism: Template-directed gap filling followed by ligation of the probe-derived strand; the paper identifies DNA polymerase and ligase for this transition.
operations.information_effect: Places a physical copy of the selected converted genomic interval within the circular probe strand. Informative bases in this copied insert report the template; synthetic probe-arm bases themselves are not measurements of the original target methylation.

operations.label: Exonuclease digestion
operations.description: Removes linear DNA after circularization, retaining circularized probe-derived capture products. The genomic-template contour shown before this step is absent afterward.
operations.mechanism: Exonuclease-mediated digestion of linear DNA after probe circularization.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplifies the retained circular capture templates with the common primer pair to yield capture amplicons. The diagram uses a repeated loop symbol for this amplified material; the source does not show a separate recircularization operation.
operations.mechanism: Common primers act through the probe-linker priming sites (P1/P2 in the diagram; AP1/AP2 in the primary Figure 1a caption).
operations.information_effect: Increases copies of the captured, conversion-coded target sequence for library construction; library molecules after PCR are copies and are not one-to-one counts of input genomic molecules.

operations.label: End repair and adaptor ligation
operations.description: The final schematic transition converts amplified capture DNA into DNA with sequencing adaptors. It explicitly labels end repair and adaptor ligation while compressing the preparation of DNA ends. The primary paper resolves this interface through fragmentation of the amplicons before end repair; see correction c_library_interface.
operations.mechanism: At the displayed block level: repair DNA ends and ligate sequencing adaptors. For the cited implementation, Figure 1d reports reamplification with dUTP, MmeI digestion and USER/S1 processing to fragment the amplicons before end repair and Solexa-adaptor ligation. The paper describes the USER/S1 approach as creating fragments with random ends. This resolves the compressed transition without adding separate unshown operations to the graph.
operations.information_effect: Adds the sequencing interface to fragments derived from the captured target copies. Conversion-dependent sequence and genomic identity, rather than the original methyl group, carry the methylation information.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, expanded BSPP row label and matching collection-page heading identify one target: bisulfite sequencing with padlock probes. All six operations belong to this row. The Deng paper supports its bisulfite-converted-template padlock capture, common-primer amplification and sequencing-library interface. The separate probe inset supplies a second material input to hybridization, rather than a product made from the converted genomic template. No alternative workflow or independent branch is retained in the BSPP row. Only the matching heading, padlock description and schematic labels of the secondary collection page support the scope; its broader catalogue claims and additional bibliography do not establish another implementation.

checks.rationale: Independent review covers all eight states, six local operations, thirteen material routes, the BSPP scope, the sole source-row paper reference and both corrections. Every BSPP transformation and its separate probe input is retained. The only multi-input operation is genuine probe/template hybridization; no independent branches are collapsed. The template-to-copy carrier change, persistence of linear template until exonuclease selection, amplification interface and final library interface agree across the connected records. No compartment, pooling, alternative method or explicit end-group chemistry is depicted and omitted. The broad final block preserves the schematic while distinguishing the paper-reported fragmentation interface. The record stops at adapter-bearing DNA; unshown routine execution and downstream analysis operations need not be added. No consequential unsupported assertion or unresolved architecture question remains.
